action_history.rationale: Model: Sum of 10 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a linear (near-zero) baseline, fit over the full range with Levenberg-Marquardt (least_squares TRF). Inventory: shoulder_128 + peak_141 (asymmetric main band), sharp peak_194, resolved 300/310 doublet, shoulder_375 + peak_395, peak_515, peak_637, peak_790. Centers bounded +/-8-10 cm-1; per-band FWHM caps (doublet <=25 cm-1); not fluorescence-dominated (rolling-min baseline area fraction = 0.206).

result.detailed_analysis: The spectrum is dominated by a very intense band at 142.18 +/- 0.01 cm-1 (relative intensity 1.0, FWHM ~8 cm-1) with a resolved low-frequency asymmetric shoulder at ~135 cm-1. This is the signature Eg mode of anatase TiO2. The remaining strong, well-constrained bands are at 395.32 +/- 0.17 cm-1 (B1g), 514.41 +/- 0.03 cm-1 (A1g/B1g overlapping pair), and 636.41 +/- 0.15 cm-1 (Eg), together with a weak band at 199 +/- 1 cm-1 (Eg). This five-band set matches the canonical anatase reference positions (144, 197, 399, 513/519, 639 cm-1) within a few cm-1, satisfying the requirement that identification rest on multiple matching positions AND their relative intensities (144 strongest, then 399/516, then 639, with 197 weak) rather than a single band. The main-band asymmetry captured by shoulder_128/shoulder_375 is consistent with instrumental/lineshape effects and possible size/strain-related broadening rather than distinct modes. The near-zero linear baseline (rolling-min area fraction 0.206) confirms the sample is not fluorescence-dominated. The fit reaches R2=0.9986 but reduced chi-square is very large (~1456) and per-band residual RMS is highest under the strongest peaks (390-540 band: ~3000-3700): these large residuals are dominated by sub-cm-1 lineshape mismatch on the tallest bands (pseudo-Voigt cannot perfectly reproduce a slightly asymmetric crystalline phonon), not by missing bands. The 300/310 doublet, 790, and possibly 194 components are weakly supported (parameters at bounds, large fractional errors) and should not be over-interpreted as physical modes; anatase has no strong canonical bands there. Machine-readable band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): [141:1.00, 395:0.70, 515:0.57, 128sh:0.42, 375sh:0.15, 637:0.093, 790:0.021, 300:0.015, 194:0.014, 310:0.010].

scientific_claims.claim: The spectrum is identified as anatase TiO2, based on four well-constrained bands at 142.18 +/- 0.01, 395.32 +/- 0.17, 514.41 +/- 0.03, and 636.41 +/- 0.15 cm-1 plus a weak 199 +/- 1 cm-1 band, matching the anatase Eg/B1g/A1g mode set within a few cm-1.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: A confident phase assignment from Raman alone constrains the TiO2 polymorph (anatase vs rutile vs brookite), which governs photocatalytic, optical, and electronic behavior; the dominant sharp Eg band at 142 and absence of rutile's 447/612 pair cleanly distinguish anatase.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed an anatase TiO2 Raman spectrum with the principal Eg mode at ~142 cm-1 and companion bands at 197, 399, 516, and 639 cm-1?
